tracks.narration: Of all the gates, just one is enough to build every digital circuit you'll ever see — which one, and why?
The NAND gate. Output is one — except when both inputs are one, in which case it drops to zero.
Tie both inputs together. Now A NAND A is the same as not A — and just like that, you have an inverter.
Feed a NAND into a NOT — also built from a NAND — and the two negations cancel. The result is plain AND. Watch the inputs cycle through every combination.
OR follows by De Morgan, and from NOT, AND, and OR you can build any Boolean expression. NAND on its own is functionally complete.
